goal: A worker-pool slot that exhausts its windowed crash-loop budget is retired in isolation while every other live member keeps running, instead of the budget being a lifetime counter that group-kills the whole pool on exhaustion.

relevant: packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- WorkerPool._supervise_tick (~line 1364) currently sets _stop_requested on exhaustion; the finally: stop() at run_supervised (~line 1343) then group-kills all members. The MAX_POOL_RESTARTS_PER_SLOT constant (~line 118) is the lifetime counter to replace.
packages/flywheel-worktree/tests/test_worker_pool.py -- keep green; test_pool_gives_up_after_restart_budget pins the old behavior and must be reconciled, not deleted, in the same change
constraints: Consume the shared windowed budget from supervision-policy-core; replace the lifetime per-slot counter (MAX_POOL_RESTARTS_PER_SLOT, never decays) with the windowed policy.
On a slot exhausting budget: retire/quarantine THAT slot only and continue supervising; do NOT set a pool-wide stop or trigger the group-kill of healthy members. Healthy members stay alive.
Preserve the orphan-free group shutdown on actual stop() (SIGTERM->SIGKILL, killpg) and the exactly-once / serialized-landing invariants -- those tests must stay green.

If an existing test asserted the old group-kill-on-exhaustion behavior, it must be updated to assert the new single-slot retirement (an equal-or-greater replacement), with its old intent re-expressed -- not silently dropped.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not change the console supervisors (separate task) or autopilot.
Do not weaken the orphan-free-shutdown or exactly-once assertions; the pool must still leave nothing alive on stop().
Do not introduce parallel landing or change the lease/claim protocol.
Do not add a process-manager dependency.
edge_cases: Pool of size >= 2: one slot crashing past budget must leave the other member's pid alive after retirement (the discriminating case).
All slots retired: the pool may now run below size N -- that is the intended trade; the pool must not crash or spin when fewer than N members are live.
Windowed budget: a slot that crashed long ago then crashes once more after the window must be respawned, not retired (no lifetime carryover).
